Session amc is confirmed. Exit window: close 2026-11-24 to close 2026-11-25.
conviction_note: The parent BBVA Group's 3Q26 report (Oct 29) shows Argentina's net attributable profit down 37% QoQ in euros (EUR 29m vs 46m), on lower recurring revenue, lower trading income and higher retail provisions. The BCRA's Q3 system ROA of 0.8%, against 2.5% in Q2, corroborates it. Both point to local net income of roughly ARS 90-105bn against a consensus near ARS 128-132bn, plus a likely cut to the 'low-teens ROE' FY26 guide. Against that: the number has been public for four weeks, Goldman is already at -27% QoQ, the ADR is down 22.6% in 20 days on Argentine politics, and last year's 40% QoQ profit collapse did not sell off. So p_up is only 43 on an abs_move of 6, giving -0.84. That is smaller than the -2.0 sum of the findings, because the reaction function and the partial pricing go into p_up.
bar: 3Q26 net income of about ARS 128-132bn (inflation-adjusted), roughly US$0.41 per ADR. Sources: FXEmpire, ARS 209.27 per share from 4 analysts, x 612.7m shares = ARS ~128bn (https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/bbar/earnings); Benzinga, US$0.41/ADR consensus, updated 2026-11-04 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BBAR/earnings-forecasts); iProfesional 2026-11-13, quoting Citi at ARS 124.49bn, which is 'about 6% below consensus', i.e. a consensus of ~ARS 132bn (https://www.iprofesional.com/finanzas/468851-wall-street-recomienda-una-sola-accion-entre-los-bancos-argentinos). Goldman, in the same article, is at -27% QoQ (~ARS 96bn, ROE 8.8%). Company FY26 guide from the 2Q26 call (2026-08-28): real ROE in the low teens, cost of risk ~6.5%, NPL ~5.5% at year-end, real loan growth ~10%, efficiency below 45%, a real NIM decline of 100-125bp (https://www.webull.com/news/15497683419390976). The two consensus sources agree within ~3%, so the bar is not capped.
positioning_check: Short interest is low and not crowded: 532,732 ADS short at the 2026-10-30 settlement (~0.26% of 204.2m ADS), days to cover 1.02, -5.5% vs Oct 15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/bbar/short-interest, fetched 2026-11-24). No squeeze mechanism. The option chain is unusable (ATM spread 116% of mid; skew null; ATM IV 86%; put/call OI 0.25), so the market makes no directional statement through options. Tape: -5.88% over 5d, -22.62% over 20d, -56.9% from the 52-week high, realised vol 48.6%. The drawdown has a sourced macro cause: doubts about Milei's re-election, country risk at 745 (highest since Oct 2025), Brazil contagion, and the August EMAE at -1.7% y/y (El Economista 2026-10-29). UBS cut its PT from US$20 to US$15 on 2026-10-19 and raised its cost of capital from 5% to 7%. Goldman is Sell with a US$11.50 PT, Citi Neutral.

findings.finding: BBVA Group's 3Q26 South America report puts Argentina's net attributable profit at EUR 29m in 3Q26 against EUR 46m in 2Q26 (-37% QoQ; 9M26 EUR 102m, -1.4% y/y). The report gives the causes as lower recurring revenue and lower net trading income, partly offset by a smaller hyperinflation charge, with provisions up on retail. Allowing for real peso depreciation in the translation, that implies BBAR's local 3Q26 net income of roughly ARS 90-105bn, against a consensus of ~ARS 128-132bn and 2Q26's ARS 131.6bn, i.e. a miss of about 20-30%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline history untrustworthy (no 6-K dates were read). Last year's analogous print: 3Q25 net income ARS 38.1bn, -39.7% QoQ, with an EPS miss ($0.50 vs $0.60 per Investing.com). Investing.com reports the ADR closed +5.56% at $14.38 after it, though the AP snapshot puts $14.38 on the release day itself, so the reaction is ambiguous (https://ng.investing.com/news/company-news/bbva-argentina-q3-2025-slides-profit-falls-40-as-loan-provisions-surge-93CH-2229424). 2Q26 beat ($0.44 vs $0.35); no sourced reaction. This name has not reliably sold off on earnings misses, and macro dominates its tape.
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly priced: the parent document has been public since Oct 29 and Goldman's -27% QoQ estimate reflects it. But the aggregated consensus (ARS ~128-132bn, roughly flat in real terms vs 2Q's 131.6bn, which is ~139bn in Sept pesos) has not moved down to it. If the market had fully priced a ~25% miss, consensus would sit near ARS 100bn rather than above Citi's 124.5bn. The ADR's 20-day fall coincides with a sector-wide political sell-off (Supervielle, Galicia and Macro all fell), so the drop does not by itself show the company-level miss is priced.
findings.independence: BCRA Informe sobre Bancos, September 2026 (published 2026-11-20): system Q3 ROA 0.8% annualised vs 2.5% in Q2, foreign-private-bank 3m ROA ~0.6%, driven by a lower margen financiero integral (https://www.bcra.gob.ar/publicaciones/informe-sobre-bancos-septiembre-de-2026/). Goldman's -27% QoQ (iProfesional, 2026-11-13). Caveat: group IFRS and euro translation differ from BCRA local GAAP; last year the group's Argentina line fell harder than the local print (group 3Q25 ~EUR 13m vs local -40% QoQ), so the local miss may be smaller than the euro figure implies.

findings.finding: System-wide Q3 profitability halved twice over: the BCRA's September Informe sobre Bancos puts the financial system's 3Q26 ROA at 0.8% annualised (ROE 3.4%), against 2.5% in 2Q26 and 1.2% for the three months to August. Foreign-owned private banks (BBVA's group) were at about 0.6% 3m ROA by September, and the decline is attributed mainly to a lower margen financiero integral. BBAR's own 2Q26 ROA was 1.8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced history of BBAR reacting to BCRA system data; the same series was public before the 3Q25 print, and the stock did not sell off on that print.
findings.why_not_priced: Published four days before the print and sector-wide, so mostly priced. It is filed as corroboration that the margin compression is systemic and not a group-accounting artefact. If it were unpriced, BBAR's consensus would sit below its 2Q level by the system's ROA decline, and it does not.
findings.independence: An independent source from finding 1 (BCRA vs the BBVA parent), pointing the same way. Supervielle 3Q26 (reported 2026-11-16): NIM -430bp QoQ to 16%, net financial income -22.4% QoQ (https://grafa.com/en/news/united-states/grupo-supervielle-q3-2026-results-net-income-falls). A proxy for BBAR, sized small.

findings.finding: The FY26 guide set on 2026-08-28 (real ROE in the low teens, cost of risk ~6.5%, real loan growth ~10%) now looks unreachable without a cut. BBAR's 1Q/2Q ROE was 8.3%/12.2%, and a ~8-9% Q3 (Goldman 8.8%) puts 9M near 10%. The parent's 9M Argentina cost of risk is 7.52% against the 6.5% FY guide. Argentina performing loans grew +23.4% YTD nominal against roughly 20% YTD inflation. Peer Supervielle cut its loan-growth guide for a fourth time on Nov 16, to flat to +5% real.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced BBAR reaction to a guidance cut. On 3Q25 management kept a positive outlook through a large miss and the stock reportedly held up. Supervielle's 4th guide cut met a +0.74% quote the next morning (grafa page, 2026-11-17), so peer guide cuts have not been punished in this tape.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: UBS cut its ROE and loan-growth estimates on Oct 19, and Goldman is Sell. If a cut to the guide were fully expected, the consensus Q4 (Benzinga $0.47/ADR) would not be above Q3; it is, which implies analysts still model a Q4 rebound toward the guide.
findings.independence: The cost-of-risk and loan figures share the parent document with finding 1 (counted once there for the quarter; here they bear only on the forward guide). Supervielle guidance cut: https://www.riotimesonline.com/grupo-supervielle-q3-earnings-2026/ (snippet). UBS estimate cuts: https://www.forbesargentina.com/money/ubs-analizo-cuatro-bancos-grandes-argentinos-recomienda-comprar-o-vender-n100664

findings.finding: Goldman's Sell on BBAR (PT cut from US$13 to US$11.50) rests on BBVA Argentina having the lowest capital ratio among the banks Goldman covers. With Q3 earnings down and loans growing 8.2% nominal in the quarter, the 3Q26 capital ratio and any dividend or capital commentary on the call are a downside line.
findings.why_not_priced: A published sell-side argument, so largely priced. Filed because the call will update the capital ratio, which a reader can measure against peers.
findings.independence: The BCRA September report shows foreign-private-bank capital integration at 24.5% of RWA against 29.0% for domestic private banks, consistent with lower capital at foreign-owned banks (same BCRA URL as finding 2, page 9). It is a system aggregate, not BBAR's own ratio.

findings.finding: Asset quality improved in Q3, as management called on 2Q: the parent reports Argentina's NPL ratio at 6.0% on 30-Sep-26, 39bp lower QoQ (BBAR local 2Q26: 6.09%), with lower NPL inflows and higher recoveries. 9M cost of risk is 7.52%, 19bp below 1H. The BCRA system's family irregularity fell to 12.20% in September (-0.61pp m/m), and the estimated default probability fell for a fourth straight month.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 3Q25 was a provisions-driven miss (NPL and cost of risk surging) and the stock reportedly held up. A peak-and-turn in NPLs is the line Argentine bank bulls cite, so it is the credibility point for management's 'Q2 was the peak' call.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Goldman expects 5.9% NPLs. Filed because it is the one line in the quarter that confirms the guide, and it offsets part of the earnings miss in how the print is read.
findings.independence: Shares the parent document with finding 1 (a different line from it). BCRA September 2026 report: system private-sector irregularity 7.50% (-0.25pp), families 12.20% (https://www.bcra.gob.ar/publicaciones/informe-sobre-bancos-septiembre-de-2026/).

findings.finding: Inflation is re-accelerating into Q4: BBVA Research estimates October national CPI at 2.2% m/m, a second monthly acceleration, and raised its 2026 inflation forecast to 31% from the ~29% BBAR's guide assumed. That raises the Q4 monetary-position loss, though it also lifts CER-linked bond income (two-thirds of BBAR's public bond book is floating/dual/Tamar-linked).
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro data, mostly priced. Filed as a small input to how the call frames the Q4 outlook; the net sign for the bank is ambiguous.
findings.independence: Proxy (macro-to-company), not confirmed by the company. Same author family as the company (BBVA Research).

rejected_candidates.detail: Folded into finding 2 (system margin compression) as independence, and its guidance cut into finding 3.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew; the 20-day run-up (-22.6%) already points down, so the negative earnings evidence agrees with the tape. That argues it is partly priced, and it moves p_up toward 50 (43 rather than ~35 on the document alone).
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): last year's -40% QoQ profit collapse reportedly did not sell off, so the reported-quarter finding went from -1.5 to -1.0 and p_up from 42 to 43.

Rule 3 (one caveat, applied once): the separate +0.5 positioning/drawdown finding was the 'partly priced' caveat to the earnings finding, so it was merged into finding 1 and moved to rejected_candidates as a duplicate.
Rule 5 (a narrow proxy loses to a broad series): the BCRA system series was cut from -0.5 to -0.3, since it is sector-wide and overlaps the company-level parent number.
Rule 3 / read the set: the guidance finding went from -1.0 to -0.8, because its cost-of-risk evidence shares the parent document with finding 1.
Inflation finding from -0.2 to -0.1 (macro-to-company transmission, ambiguous sign).

Rule 6: the bar is verified by two roughly agreeing consensus sources (FXEmpire ~ARS 128bn, Citi-implied ~ARS 132bn), so no cap. Rule 7: short interest was checked and is low, so there is no squeeze adjustment.
